prompt: RimWorld creature sprite, side view, flat cel-shaded vanilla-RimWorld toy-figurine art style: the Pyrelands' fire-hawk -- a lean raptor that carries a burning twig from one fire to the next to spread the burn deliberately, flushing prey ahead of the flame-line. Vivid ASH-GREY plumage with bold EMBER-ORANGE wing and tail markings, a hooked beak, one wing held slightly open as its identity feature (wings stay prominent, simple and jointless -- alert but calm, never mid-flight). Single creature, centered, calm standing pose, no ground shadow, no background scenery. Heavy, clean black outline around the whole silhouette and all major internal linework, thick enough to read clearly at standard RimWorld zoom and below. Toy-figurine convention, strict: calm neutral standing pose -- never mid-stride, stooping or diving; pure flat side profile with no three-quarter perspective; no visible musculature, feather-tract or anatomy detail; flat cel shading with large simple color areas and minimal surface texture, clean vanilla-RimWorld style. Leg policy, strict RimWorld dialect: legs (other than the wings) are used SPARINGLY. Show at most TWO short, thick stub legs, with the far-side leg hidden inside the body mass; leg length at most one quarter of the body height; no joints, no talons detailed beyond a simple rounded nub. Only the wings are the exception to the leg/limb budget and may stay full-size, simple and jointless.
style_notes: v2: re-render of our own RUT_FireHawk under the toy-figurine law.
